sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: Two day Tribunals reveal you and allow immediate executions on nomination, normally up to two victims. Reveals and wills are delayed until it ends.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Town by eliminating opposing factions; the role’s ability is a tool toward that shared objective.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Jesters and Executioners interact with Tribunal deaths; modifiers can change trial capacity. Your bonus vote is tied to the active Tribunal.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: A Tribunal is a public demonstration, not proof your targets are evil. Lack of intermediate flips makes the second execution particularly risky.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not activate just to confirm yourself. Do not expect immediate feedback after the first victim. Do not use an outdated three-execution default.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Keep exact identity concealed where useful until the public ability’s benefit warrants revealing.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Collect evidence rather than Tribunaling solely to reveal.
- **Middle:** Prepare a coherent two-target plan before activation.
- **Late:** Check whether an opposing voting bloc would control the accelerated executions.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: Two supported contradictions exist and allies can coordinate: plan both nominations before starting the Tribunal.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You have no ordinary N1 action. Prepare a short list of unresolved claims and the evidence you would need before starting a Tribunal.

**How to choose:** Read D1 for contradictions and useful claims. With no evidence, write “No case yet” and save the ability; the absence of an opening target is normal.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Build one evidence-backed case. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Collect deaths and investigative posts into separate cases. A Tribunal increases voting capacity; it does not tell you which players are evil.

**What this does and does not establish:** A Tribunal is a public demonstration, not proof your targets are evil. Lack of intermediate flips makes the second execution particularly risky.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
There is still no night button to use. Review the outcome of D2 votes and prepare one question for each surviving case. Reassess numbers before a later Tribunal rather than carrying a failed push forward unchanged.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Collect evidence rather than Tribunaling solely to reveal.
- **Middle:** Prepare a coherent two-target plan before activation.
- **Late:** Check whether an opposing voting bloc would control the accelerated executions.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not activate just to confirm yourself. Do not expect immediate feedback after the first victim. Do not use an outdated three-execution default.

**Important interaction:** Jesters and Executioners interact with Tribunal deaths; modifiers can change trial capacity. Your bonus vote is tied to the active Tribunal.

**Worked decision:** Two supported contradictions exist and allies can coordinate: plan both nominations before starting the Tribunal.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You have no N1 action and cannot reveal on D1. Prepare to compare D2 claims and keep your reveal for a useful voting decision.

**How to choose:** Note who makes a concrete claim and who simply repeats a push. If D1 offers nothing, leave the suspect list blank; do not manufacture a target to feel active.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Keep a clear evidence list. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Read the new information before deciding whether revealing would change a vote. Surviving N1 does not confirm anyone who says they protected you.

**What this does and does not establish:** Extra votes do not establish that your social reads are correct. Custom faction/conversion rules require separate allegiance reasoning.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Wait for a useful death and collect an actual autopsy.
- **Middle:** Build multiple relevant killer records and examine plausible candidates.
- **Late:** Explain exactly what a negative examination excludes; accumulated records still are not a global role check.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
In an ordinary start there is no eligible autopsy yet, so you have no useful N1 examination. Prepare a corpse-to-killer record instead of inventing a result.

**How to choose:** At D2, inspect the graveyard for an eligible autopsy. Choose a death whose killer record could answer an unresolved case. If no suitable body exists, record that limitation.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Create an eligible autopsy record. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the death information separately from your own later examination. The killer shown by an autopsy is not a numbered player identification.

**What this does and does not establish:** No match means no match to collected killer records, not globally innocent. A true role result does not automatically establish faction or voluntary guilt.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
After a valid autopsy, examine an eligible living suspect and record Match/No Match or the actual failure feedback. A No Match excludes only the killer records your examination covers, not every evil role.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Wait for a useful death and collect an actual autopsy.
- **Middle:** Build multiple relevant killer records and examine plausible candidates.
- **Late:** Explain exactly what a negative examination excludes; accumulated records still are not a global role check.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Watch one eligible house for visible visitors. Choose the house for the information its traffic might provide.

**How to choose:** A credible player expected to attract visits can be informative, but an obvious crowded call also risks rampages. With no reliable claim, watch an eligible unknown; avoid assuming a loud TP/LO call is safe or truthful.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Get one correctly directed visitor list. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record who visited the watched player, not whom that player visited. An empty visible visitor list and a failed watch are different. Astral actions can be absent from the list.

**What this does and does not establish:** A visitor list is not a killer list. No visible visitors does not exclude astral effects or establish that the target was safe.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If D2 reveals a threatened useful ally or a disputed visitor story, watch the house that can resolve that question. If your previous target had no useful traffic, choose a new house instead of treating the first choice as permanent.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Watch a plausible useful target while accounting for visitor hazards.
- **Middle:** Use known traffic and claims to test who explains reported effects.
- **Late:** Choose the house whose traffic would most resolve the remaining uncertainty, not simply the loudest player.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
On standard N1, choose one eligible player for a Good vision containing two names. The chosen player is included; record both names.

**How to choose:** A genuinely suspicious selected player can make the other name more useful, but suspicion is not proof. With no D1 evidence, choose an eligible unknown and treat the resulting pair as a starting lead only.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Publish a complete labeled vision. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Write “Good: [two names]; selected [name]” or the actual failure. At least one is classified Good under the current effects; that does not establish that the other is Evil.

**What this does and does not establish:** At least one is a group condition, not exactly one. Do not identify a single culprit without additional evidence.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
On the standard even-night Evil vision, select an independently supported Town reference if one exists, and record all three names. If none is established, select an eligible unknown and keep all members unresolved. Check the night’s actual vision mode.

- **Early:** Report the first Good pair without overclearing either name.
- **Middle:** Use established references where legal and resolve earlier visions.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Check an unresolved player; establish a prompt reporting habit.
- **Middle:** Compare results with the evolving faction threats rather than repeatedly checking plausible innocents.
- **Late:** Combine vote math, claims, and exceptions; an innocent result still cannot solve the endgame alone.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Search one eligible unresolved player. Your result will be Innocent or Suspicious if the check resolves normally.

**How to choose:** Prefer a player whose claim or action can be questioned tomorrow. With no useful D1 information, choose an eligible unknown outside obvious Veteran bait. Quietness alone is not evidence of evil.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Publish one honest check. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the literal result. Innocent leaves the bookholder and several other evil roles possible; Suspicious can be caused by framing. A failed search is neither result.

**What this does and does not establish:** Innocent leaves many evils possible, including Neutral Killings and the bookholder. Suspicious can come from framing, and identifies more than Coven.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Check a new unresolved player whose D2 story matters. A roleblocked N1 gives you no check to build on; retry only if the target still deserves priority. Do not spend the game clearing everyone based on Innocent.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Check an unresolved player; establish a prompt reporting habit.
- **Middle:** Compare results with the evolving faction threats rather than repeatedly checking plausible innocents.
- **Late:** Combine vote math, claims, and exceptions; an innocent result still cannot solve the endgame alone.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.markdown:
Guard one eligible player against an interceptable harmful visitor, if the ability is enabled. You are not granting an ordinary healing barrier.

**How to choose:** Prefer a credible useful ally who is plausibly threatened by a direct visitor. With no reliable claim, choose an eligible unknown without calling them confirmed, or conserve self-protection unless you have a concrete personal threat.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose a reasoned protection target. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the guard attempt and any actual interception feedback. An uneventful night is not a save. Your death or their survival does not prove their faction, and astral or additional attacks can bypass the plan.

**What this does and does not establish:** A guard attempt is not a save. A death despite your guard can involve additional attacks or an astral bypass.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If D2 exposes a valuable ally threatened by a direct attack, consider guarding them and coordinating credible protection on yourself. If the expected threat is astral, revise the plan rather than promising an interception.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Protect a credible useful ally rather than a random loud claim.
- **Middle:** Coordinate protection on yourself if an interception is likely.
- **Late:** Consider the actual remaining attack types before sacrificing yourself for a role whose ability may be spent.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not say you grant a normal barrier. Do not expect to stop all attacks. Do not assume dying to protect someone proves their faction.

**Important interaction:** Barrier protection can preserve you during a counterattack. Astral attacks bypass interception; Shroud can make an otherwise friendly visitor harmful.

**Worked decision:** A revealed leader is threatened by ordinary killing: guarding them may trade your life for theirs, whereas an expected astral attack calls for another plan.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game

These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Middle:** Coordinate a valuable low-traffic protection target.
- **Late:** Choose protection that preserves the necessary vote while reducing allied visitor casualties.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Fortify one eligible player while remembering that your ability can attack a visitor, including a Town visitor.

**How to choose:** Prefer a credible useful ally away from an obvious crowded call. With no reliable opening target, choose a less congested eligible house or hold if the collateral risk is unjustified; ask for coordination rather than visiting a pile blindly.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Protect without inviting a Town pileup. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record your target and actual attack/protection feedback. A visitor’s death does not prove they were evil, and your selected target is not automatically confirmed by receiving defense.

**What this does and does not establish:** Your attack does not identify an evil visitor. Failure to kill can reflect defense rather than the absence of a visitor.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If D2 provides a better protection target, move with a reason and consider who will visit. If your prior fortification killed a Town visitor, change the traffic plan instead of repeating it mechanically.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Avoid uncontrolled crowded protection calls.
- **Middle:** Coordinate a valuable low-traffic protection target.
- **Late:** Choose protection that preserves the necessary vote while reducing allied visitor casualties.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

**How to choose:** Read D1 for a concrete contradiction worth asking about tomorrow. With no information, leave your target undecided. “No target yet” is correct; a quiet player or a request to prove yourself is not a shooting case.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Build one supported case before shooting. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete opening, with no forced shot

**Setup:** You are Deputy in the normal text profile. D1 has no useful claims. You have not used High Noon.

1. **N1:** No ability target is required. Start an action line, `N1: No night ability`, and a separate question list. Do not select someone merely to fill a box.
2. **D2:** Suppose #6 posts `Tracker: N1 #9 -> #4`, while #9 claims `Veteran, stayed home; no role change`. Ask #9 to explain that specific movement conflict. Check for redirection, role changes, mistaken identity, or a false Tracker before treating it as settled. This is a case to investigate, not an automatic shooting instruction.
3. **Public alignment:** If the lobby asks for alignment, answer `TK`. If explaining the full role is useful, say `Deputy; shot unused`. Neither TP nor TS is correct for your actual role.
4. **Decision:** If the case remains unresolved, hold the shot. If independent evidence supports an enemy, the day ability is enabled, nobody is on the stand, and using the shot has value, consider it. One shot is available; using it to prove yourself can waste it.
5. **Outcome branch:** Suppose you fire and get Miss. Log `D2: Shot 9 — Miss`. The charge is spent. A Town target, sufficient defense, or other relevant context can explain the miss; do not announce `9 confirmed Town`.
6. **N2:** Still no night ability. If the bullet remains, update the case. If spent, use claims, questions, and votes rather than waiting for another bullet.

**What the beginner can now answer:** Do I have an N1 button? No. What is useful instead? Prepare an honest history and a specific follow-up. What do I claim? TK. Must I shoot D2? No. Does a miss clear the target? No.

**Why this is useful:** It replaces an impossible first-night action with a legitimate preparation task and explains the irreversible decision before the player spends the charge. Success for this lesson is a reasoned hold or supported shot, not a required kill.

These are recommendations, not forced actions:

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You have no night ability. Save your single day shot and prepare to question D2 claims; you cannot shoot on D1.

**How to choose:** Read D1 for a concrete contradiction worth asking about tomorrow. With no information, leave your target undecided. “No target yet” is correct; a quiet player or a request to prove yourself is not a shooting case.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Build one supported case before shooting. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete opening, with no forced shot

**Setup:** You are Deputy in the normal text profile. D1 has no useful claims. You have not used High Noon.

1. **N1:** No ability target is required. Start an action line, `N1: No night ability`, and a separate question list. Do not select someone merely to fill a box.
2. **D2:** Suppose #6 posts `Tracker: N1 #9 -> #4`, while #9 claims `Veteran, stayed home; no role change`. Ask #9 to explain that specific movement conflict. Check for redirection, role changes, mistaken identity, or a false Tracker before treating it as settled. This is a case to investigate, not an automatic shooting instruction.
3. **Public alignment:** If the lobby asks for alignment, answer `TK`. If explaining the full role is useful, say `Deputy; shot unused`. Neither TP nor TS is correct for your actual role.
4. **Decision:** If the case remains unresolved, hold the shot. If independent evidence supports an enemy, the day ability is enabled, nobody is on the stand, and using the shot has value, consider it. One shot is available; using it to prove yourself can waste it.
5. **Outcome branch:** Suppose you fire and get Miss. Log `D2: Shot 9 — Miss`. The charge is spent. A Town target, sufficient defense, or other relevant context can explain the miss; do not announce `9 confirmed Town`.
6. **N2:** Still no night ability. If the bullet remains, update the case. If spent, use claims, questions, and votes rather than waiting for another bullet.

**What the beginner can now answer:** Do I have an N1 button? No. What is useful instead? Prepare an honest history and a specific follow-up. What do I claim? TK. Must I shoot D2? No. Does a miss clear the target? No.

**Why this is useful:** It replaces an impossible first-night action with a legitimate preparation task and explains the irreversible decision before the player spends the charge. Success for this lesson is a reasoned hold or supported shot, not a required kill.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Write “N1: No night ability.” Collect D2 claims and results before deciding about the shot. A night death is not evidence you personally tested anyone.

**What this does and does not establish:** A miss does not prove the target is Town. Another player can falsely claim credit for a public shot.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
There is still no night action. If you held the shot, reassess the case after D2 and new results. If you used it, record hit/miss and keep contributing with votes and questions; the bullet does not replenish.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Preserve the lone shot until a supported target exists.
- **Middle:** Use it where it meaningfully changes the evidence or vote.
- **Late:** A remaining shot can be decisive, but defense means a miss does not establish Town.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not use outdated shoot-Town-and-die rules. Do not expect multiple bullets. Do not treat a private miss as hard confirmation.

**Important interaction:** Enchant/Reap can change eligibility. Early Neutral Evil defense and other protection can explain a miss.

**Worked decision:** D2 shot at #7 misses: report the attempt if needed, but keep #7 unresolved rather than declaring them safe.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Load on N1. You cannot shoot on the first night, so your job is to prepare a supported target rather than firing.

**How to choose:** No shooting target is required for the loading action. Note one question for D2 and leave the suspect list blank if D1 supplies nothing. Loading and choosing a later target are separate decisions.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Complete the first Load. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record whether loading completed and your actual ammunition state. Do not write a shot or a killed target for a night spent loading.

**What this does and does not establish:** A failed shot does not uniquely identify natural defense. An Investigator finding Murder on a shooting night need not have found an evil.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If loaded and a supported target exists, consider a legal shot. If the case is weak, hold or Load within the limit. Shooting Town loses the gun under current rules; do not use old suicide advice or assume unlimited ammunition.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Load and build a supported suspect list.
- **Middle:** Alternate useful shots with necessary loading and count ammunition.
- **Late:** Consider whether shooting changes the next vote; do not fire simply because a bullet remains.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You do not manually pick a corpse on N1. Wait for the automatic Remember process and prepare to switch plans if you acquire an eligible Town role.

**How to choose:** No numbered night target is needed. Read D1 claims and keep notes that will remain useful after a role change; do not promise a specific inherited role.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Observe the actual Remember. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Check the actual new role notification. If no eligible Remember occurred, stay on the Amnesiac plan. Preserve the night history rather than rewriting N1 as an action from the newly acquired role.

**What this does and does not establish:** A hidden or altered death does not necessarily prevent Remember. Multiple Amnesiacs cannot all acquire the same Unique role.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Open the acquired role’s current action instructions. If still Amnesiac, there is no manual resurrection to perform. If transformed into an action role, start from its actual available state and phase.

- **Early:** Learn claims while awaiting an eligible automatic Remember.
- **Middle:** After transition, follow the new role’s strategy and retain the old-role history.

sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: Drink with a player to roleblock their night ability. Successful roleblocking leaves Hangover, preventing immediate repeat blocking; you are roleblock immune.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Town by eliminating opposing factions; the role’s ability is a tool toward that shared objective.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits

sections.title: Common mistakes

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Find a reasoned disruption target.
- **Middle:** Use target feedback, claim conflicts, and Hangover to plan new blocks.
- **Late:** Distinguish preventing a lethal action from merely seeking a reassuring no-kill night.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: N1 block #4 and no kill occurs: ask for #4’s action and seek corroboration instead of calling the case solved.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Drink with one eligible player to attempt a roleblock. This disrupts an action; it does not investigate their faction.

**How to choose:** Prefer a player whose claimed or suspected night action makes disruption useful. With no D1 lead, choose an eligible unknown away from obvious dangerous visitor bait. Roleblocking certain killers, including an uncautious Serial Killer, can be dangerous.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Get one honest disruption record. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record your target and actual feedback, then compare it with what they report. No deaths elsewhere does not prove you blocked a killer. A failed block is not a successful Drink.

**What this does and does not establish:** No kill after a block is a lead, not proof of the killer. A target’s immunity or Hangover can explain a failed block.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Choose a different eligible player after a successful Drink because Hungover prevents a consecutive block. Use D2 evidence to disrupt a meaningful action; do not promise to lock the same person indefinitely.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Find a reasoned disruption target.
- **Middle:** Use target feedback, claim conflicts, and Hangover to plan new blocks.
- **Late:** Distinguish preventing a lethal action from merely seeking a reassuring no-kill night.

sections.title: Win condition

Win with Town by eliminating opposing factions; the role’s ability is a tool toward that shared objective.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Learn the deck, claims, and voting rhythm.
- **Middle:** Ask specific questions and organize contradictions honestly.
- **Late:** Explain vote choices from public evidence; do not invent night proof to compensate for lacking an ability.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You have no special night ability. Your useful N1 work is reading claims and preparing to compare D2 evidence.

**How to choose:** No target is required. With no D1 information, leave the suspect list open; neither silence nor having no button means you must invent an investigative story.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Keep an honest action history. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Log no role action and read the graveyard and TI posts. You have not personally cleared anyone by surviving.

**What this does and does not establish:** No action supplies no investigative result. Your social reads should remain visibly separate from claimed mechanical facts.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
You still have no night action. Update your notes with claim changes, votes, and contradictions so you can help choose a supported vote on the next day.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Learn the deck, claims, and voting rhythm.
- **Middle:** Ask specific questions and organize contradictions honestly.
- **Late:** Explain vote choices from public evidence; do not invent night proof to compensate for lacking an ability.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Current CPOW roles are mutually exclusive at normal spawning. Self-retraining and known-ally restrictions need separate treatment.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: Retraining changes role, not automatically faction. It can invalidate a role reveal or cover plan made earlier.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not use the old two-retrain or Basic Defense model. Do not assume every role is available. Do not claim you retrained and independently attacked normally.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Use a sustainable Town cover; absent book or retraining, nonvisiting claims may fit. Avoid asserting a protective effect you cannot reproduce.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Assess which roles the faction needs.
- **Middle:** Retrain only where the new ability has a practical purpose.
- **Late:** Prefer the action that can change the next vote/kill rather than a late transformation with no time to help.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: A needed utility role is available: agree the change with your ally and retain a dated old-role/new-role history.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Check who holds the Necronomicon. If it is you, plan the team’s enabled book attack; Retrain is an alternative decision, not a free extra attack.

**How to choose:** Coordinate with the visible Coven roster before acting. For a kill, choose a nonally with useful enemy value while avoiding obvious protected/visitor-trap targets. With no lead, choose a legal nonally rather than a teammate; do not randomly Retrain a useful ally.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Coordinate the first team action. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the actual action, destination, and feedback in private. A failed kill can involve defense or interruption; it is not an exact role identification.

**What this does and does not establish:** Retraining changes role, not automatically faction. It can invalidate a role reveal or cover plan made earlier.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If the kill was stopped, compare feedback and team information before retrying. Retrain only to solve a team need, with the attack tradeoff understood. Recheck book ownership and the effect on your cover each night.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Assess which roles the faction needs.
- **Middle:** Retrain only where the new ability has a practical purpose.
- **Late:** Prefer the action that can change the next vote/kill rather than a late transformation with no time to help.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Psychic (TI): visiting fallback before book; Oracle (TP): conditional fit with book. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Psychic — TI (Town Investigative); Visiting fallback before book.** An ordinary direct Hex can match one chosen visited player. **What can expose it:** You have no genuine vision; the night parity and full group constraint still need a plausible story.

**Oracle — TP (Town Protective); Conditional fit with book.** The astral book Hex/attack avoids a normal direct visit. **What can expose it:** There is no real Aegis, and pre-book direct visits may conflict with an all-Oracle history.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: One Powerful meteor during a later day; your identity is not publicly announced by the ability. With book, you can also make ordinary night attacks.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: The meteor has different strength and feedback from a basic shot. Secret Killers does not justify assuming every cinematic disappears.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: A public meteor announces the ability occurred, not which living player used it.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not assume night barriers persist into daytime. Do not claim a public reveal ability you cannot demonstrate. Do not use the meteor on an invulnerable target casually.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Before book, nonvisiting covers may match movement. A meteor cannot pass as a Deputy shot with a different visible event.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Keep the meteor until a valuable opportunity.
- **Middle:** Remove a consequential target when it changes control.
- **Late:** Do not die holding it merely out of habit; assess defense and the immediate vote state.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: A confirmed leader threatens a decisive vote: assess whether meteor removal changes the outcome before spending it.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You cannot Meteor on D1. At night, use the book attack only if you hold it and the setup enables it; otherwise prepare your cover and later day target.

**How to choose:** With no book, there is no extra N1 attack to invent. Note a possible later high-value enemy, then wait for evidence. With the book, coordinate a legal nonally target and the team’s other visits.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Keep day and night actions distinct. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Log the actual book action or no role action. Your future Meteor is a separate day ability and does not explain an ordinary N1 death by itself.

**What this does and does not establish:** A public meteor announces the ability occurred, not which living player used it.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Recheck book ownership. Save or use the later day Meteor for a concrete faction benefit, then keep its charge state distinct from night attacks. Do not claim a second Meteor after spending it.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Keep the meteor until a valuable opportunity.
- **Middle:** Remove a consequential target when it changes control.
- **Late:** Do not die holding it merely out of habit; assess defense and the immediate vote state.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not assume night barriers persist into daytime. Do not claim a public reveal ability you cannot demonstrate. Do not use the meteor on an invulnerable target casually.

**Important interaction:** The meteor has different strength and feedback from a basic shot. Secret Killers does not justify assuming every cinematic disappears.

**Worked decision:** A confirmed leader threatens a decisive vote: assess whether meteor removal changes the outcome before spending it.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Oracle (TP): conditional astral fit; Deputy (TK): difficult demonstration claim. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Oracle — TP (Town Protective); Conditional astral fit.** A ritual or inactive night can fit a no-visible-visit cover. **What can expose it:** No actual Aegis is supplied; direct book attacks can conflict.

**Deputy — TK (Town Killing); Difficult demonstration claim.** Neither role requires an ordinary N1 visit. **What can expose it:** Town may reasonably ask for the one day shot, which you cannot perform.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Illumination lasts conditionally and matters to target eligibility. Ordinary book attacks and Blood Ritual are alternative actions.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: A wrong guess spends a charge without proving the target’s alternate role. Your private role certainty is not a result an Oracle could report.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not use old three-charge or public-failure-exposure rules. Do not guess TIs. Do not assume a Potion Master reveal immediately supplies a usable ritual target.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Oracle is a movement-compatible cover while using astral rituals, but lacks real protective feedback and becomes weaker after a normal book attack.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Collect exact eligible role knowledge without wasting guesses.
- **Middle:** Spend attempts on supported targets after checking Illumination.
- **Late:** Choose ritual or ordinary attack based on remaining defenses and win requirements.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: A public eligible exact role is known: check defenses and Illumination before committing one of only two attempts.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
If you do not have a well-supported eligible role guess, hold the Ritual. You have two attempts and cannot guess TI; a fresh N1 often lacks useful evidence.

**How to choose:** Use an exact supported role claim or team-provided role knowledge only after checking eligibility and Illuminated status. With no evidence, do not spend a guess on a random number/role pair. A book attack is a separate alternative.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Preserve both attempts without evidence. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the actual outcome and remaining attempts. A wrong guess does not produce the old public exposure event; lack of that event is not proof your guess was correct.

**What this does and does not establish:** A wrong guess spends a charge without proving the target’s alternate role. Your private role certainty is not a result an Oracle could report.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Use D2 claims and Coven information for a legal exact guess. If no supported guess exists, hold again or use the available book alternative. Do not force a TI or Illuminated target into the selector.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Collect exact eligible role knowledge without wasting guesses.
- **Middle:** Spend attempts on supported targets after checking Illumination.
- **Late:** Choose ritual or ordinary attack based on remaining defenses and win requirements.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

Do not use old three-charge or public-failure-exposure rules. Do not guess TIs. Do not assume a Potion Master reveal immediately supplies a usable ritual target.

**Crusader — TP (Town Protective); Partial effect fit; difficult.** Both can create danger for visitors at a chosen house. **What can expose it:** Jinx supplies no Crusader defense; death details and surviving witnesses can identify you.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Choose traffic carefully to limit identity exposure.
- **Middle:** Exploit useful visitors while planning for survivors who can report you.
- **Late:** Judge whether an extra visitor kill outweighs being identified before the final vote.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Jinx an eligible house to attack a visitor if the action is enabled. You do not grant Crusader-style defense to the resident.

**How to choose:** Choose a nonally house likely to draw useful enemy visitors, while coordinating to keep Coven away. With no useful traffic plan, holding can be better than exposing yourself to surviving witnesses. The normal visitor attack excludes Coven allies. Grace Period may disable the harmful action.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Plan around visitor traffic. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record actual attack feedback and remember that surviving witnesses can expose you. Do not turn the action into a complete visitor list or claim the house owner received protection.

**What this does and does not establish:** Knowing that you attacked a visitor is not a complete visitor list. A survivor can carry evidence against you even if nobody dies.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If exposed, revise the survival plan rather than continuing a supposed safe protective routine. If not exposed, choose a useful house using D2 traffic and avoid allied visitors; recheck whether the book changes your action.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Choose traffic carefully to limit identity exposure.
- **Middle:** Exploit useful visitors while planning for survivors who can report you.
- **Late:** Judge whether an extra visitor kill outweighs being identified before the final vote.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not label Jinx→Lookout a natural full-information fit. Do not assume all visitors die. Do not use crowded protection calls without understanding exposure.

**Important interaction:** Astral visitors evade the passive attack. With book, the direct attack creates additional interception risks.

**Worked decision:** You expect one protector on #4: compare the possible kill with the risk of that protector surviving and reporting you.

sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: Three Stone Gazes mark players so their eventual death role and will are hidden from opponents. Medusa begins self-Stoned; book can attack while applying Stone.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Necromancer can use Stoned bodies; normal Town Retributionist cannot. Amnesiac can remember underlying roles.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: Coven may learn information opponents cannot read. It should not appear in a claimed Town will without a legitimate explanation.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not use the old stay-home visitor-petrification ability. Do not assume Stone kills. Do not assume hidden bodies prevent every role from learning their truth.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: A visiting cover fits movement better than an inherently nonvisiting one while gazing. Claiming a hidden role is conditional, not automatically safe.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Suppress meaningful information rather than marking random expendable players.
- **Middle:** Use hidden information to plan without leaking it through an incompatible cover.
- **Late:** Retain role-space uncertainty where useful, but account for true-role recovery by other abilities.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: A useful opponent is expected to die: Stone can suppress their public will, but surviving targets remain marked for later.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Stonemark an eligible player if doing so has a useful concealment purpose. You have three active-use charges; starting self-Stone is not an extra chosen target.

**How to choose:** Prefer a target whose later hidden death information helps the team, and coordinate with likely kills. With no concrete plan, holding a charge is reasonable. The mark persists; you do not need to spend one nightly by habit.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose a useful concealment target. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the applied mark or failure and remaining charges. A mark does not kill the target immediately; the book adds a distinct attack effect.

**What this does and does not establish:** Coven may learn information opponents cannot read. It should not appear in a claimed Town will without a legitimate explanation.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Reassess living marked players and expected deaths. Mark another useful target or hold; with the book, account for the attack and its visible consequences in the cover story.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Suppress meaningful information rather than marking random expendable players.
- **Middle:** Use hidden information to plan without leaking it through an incompatible cover.
- **Late:** Retain role-space uncertainty where useful, but account for true-role recovery by other abilities.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not use the old stay-home visitor-petrification ability. Do not assume Stone kills. Do not assume hidden bodies prevent every role from learning their truth.

**Important interaction:** Necromancer can use Stoned bodies; normal Town Retributionist cannot. Amnesiac can remember underlying roles.

**Worked decision:** A useful opponent is expected to die: Stone can suppress their public will, but surviving targets remain marked for later.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: A corpse visit and generated effect may support a corpse-user claim, but do not establish Town faction.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not claim Town Ret while using a Stoned/evil corpse or self-protection normally forbidden to Ret. Do not claim simultaneous ordinary reanimation and book attack.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Retributionist is a natural conditional cover only while using actions, bodies, and targets a genuine Town Ret could use.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Watch for suitable bodies and avoid promising an unavailable action.
- **Middle:** Exploit corpse utility while keeping any Ret story inside legal bounds.
- **Late:** Compare the best corpse effect with a direct book attack; ordinary nights do not allow both.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: Use a legal dead Town investigator on #9 and preserve the real returned information; an evil corpse kill would require a different explanation.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
In an ordinary fresh game there is no corpse to reanimate. Use a book attack only if you hold the book and it is enabled; otherwise prepare for the graveyard.

**How to choose:** No corpse should be invented on N1. At D2, inspect actual dead roles and their permitted abilities. If holding the book, coordinate a legal nonally attack instead of claiming simultaneous normal reanimation.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Inspect the real graveyard. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record no eligible corpse or the actual book result. Keep real corpse eligibility and uses separate from any Retributionist cover draft.

**What this does and does not establish:** A corpse visit and generated effect may support a corpse-user claim, but do not establish Town faction.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
If a usable corpse exists, choose its ability for the team’s current need and log the borrowed result privately. If no compatible Town corpse exists, do not fabricate one for a Ret story; the book is an alternative action.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Watch for suitable bodies and avoid promising an unavailable action.
- **Middle:** Exploit corpse utility while keeping any Ret story inside legal bounds.
- **Late:** Compare the best corpse effect with a direct book attack; ordinary nights do not allow both.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not claim Town Ret while using a Stoned/evil corpse or self-protection normally forbidden to Ret. Do not claim simultaneous ordinary reanimation and book attack.

**Important interaction:** Necromancer takes corpse-use priority over Ret. Some day-role bodies act at the next appropriate transition.

**Worked decision:** Use a legal dead Town investigator on #9 and preserve the real returned information; an evil corpse kill would require a different explanation.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

cards.title: First night: action and target
cards.compact: Check the book first. Without it, ordinary Drink is the simpler opening: attempt to roleblock one useful nonally. Smog is a different ability, not another name for Drink. Coordinate to avoid blocking an ally or obstructing allied visits.
cards.expanded:
Check the book first. Without it, ordinary Drink is the simpler opening: attempt to roleblock one useful nonally. Smog is a different ability, not another name for Drink.

**How to choose:** Coordinate to avoid blocking an ally or obstructing allied visits. Prefer a suspected useful enemy night actor; with no role evidence, choose an eligible nonally away from obvious visitor traps. Drinking with an uncautious Serial Killer can be dangerous.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose a mode with a reason. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete Drink → cover → rotate sequence

**Setup:** You are Poisoner, actually CU. Another Coven member has the book. #4 is an eligible nonally; Coven has no plan requiring #4 to act. There is no known dangerous visitor bait. These are example facts, not facts the site knows about a live match.

1. **N1 mode:** Choose ordinary Drink on #4 for a simple disruption plan. If no enemy role is known, choose an eligible unknown nonally; the choice is not a prediction that they must be a TI or killer. Check team plans first.
2. **Private record:** Write `N1: Drink 4 — [actual feedback]`. If interrupted, keep that outcome. Do not fill “success” just because you pressed the ability.
3. **Public cover:** Select **Tavern Keeper — TS** from the unrestricted claim selector. This is logical because the target can genuinely experience a roleblock, which the cover can produce. If a full claim is requested, a compatible deliberately authored public history is `Tavern Keeper / N1: Drink 4`. Do not copy the private Poisoner heading or faction information.
4. **D2 interpretation:** If #4 reports being roleblocked, that supports the action account; it does not prove you are Tavern Keeper or Town. If they report a different effect, do not silently alter your own private action record to fit them.
5. **N2 after successful Drink:** #4 is Hungover. Choose a different useful eligible target, such as an independently identified enemy night actor. Do not promise to roleblock #4 on consecutive nights.
6. **Alternative mode:** Smog blocks incoming visits to the selected house with an obstacle effect; it does not simply stop the owner’s action. Coordinate because allied visits can also be obstructed. Socialite — TS becomes an explainable but difficult alternative, with guest-list and immunity differences. Keeping Tavern Keeper while claiming every Smog report was a roleblock creates a mismatch.
7. **Book branch:** If you receive the book, the direct attack also roleblocks. Do not plan a normal book attack plus Smog together. A dead target and a genuine roleblock effect can change how well the old cover survives.

**What the beginner can now answer:** Which button starts the simple plan? Drink. Who is a legal fallback? A nonally, after checking team interference and visiting danger. What alignment goes public? TS for the Tavern Keeper cover, not actual CU. Who next? A new eligible target after successful Drink. Is Smog the same effect? No.

**Why this cover has a reason:** It matches target feedback as well as an ordinary visit. **Why it is not guaranteed:** A real effect does not establish faction; mode changes, Hangover, the book, and independent observations can expose differences. Cleric remains selectable as TP, but supplies a weaker story because you do not actually Barrier and the target may report disruption.

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Tavern Keeper (TS): natural effect fit on drink; Socialite (TS): partial effect fit; difficult on smog; Cleric (TP): unrestricted but weak fallback. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Tavern Keeper — TS (Town Support); Natural effect fit on Drink.** Drink can create the same roleblock effect the target expects from a Tavern Keeper. **What can expose it:** Hungover prevents a repeat lock; Smog is an obstacle effect, and book attacks add lethal consequences.

**Socialite — TS (Town Support); Partial effect fit; difficult on Smog.** Smog and a Party can both obstruct access to a house. **What can expose it:** Socialite has invitations, different immunity rules, and a different legal house sequence; resemblance is incomplete.

**Cleric — TP (Town Protective); Unrestricted but weak fallback.** An ordinary direct visit can be written as a claimed Barrier destination. **What can expose it:** Drink or Smog feedback does not match pure protection, and you provide no genuine Barrier.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

cards.title: Mistakes and important interactions
cards.compact: Do not use outdated delayed-poison advice. Do not conflate Drink with Smog. Do not claim a roleblock lock through Hangover.
cards.expanded:
Do not use outdated delayed-poison advice. Do not conflate Drink with Smog. Do not claim a roleblock lock through Hangover.

**Important interaction:** Real Socialites and Spies can expose Smog-based stories. Some Coven astral interactions differ from ordinary astral bypass.

**Worked decision:** N1 Drink #4 supports a Tavern Keeper will; choosing Smog N2 means the story must account for a different effect.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Check the book first. Without it, ordinary Drink is the simpler opening: attempt to roleblock one useful nonally. Smog is a different ability, not another name for Drink.

**How to choose:** Coordinate to avoid blocking an ally or obstructing allied visits. Prefer a suspected useful enemy night actor; with no role evidence, choose an eligible nonally away from obvious visitor traps. Drinking with an uncautious Serial Killer can be dangerous.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose a mode with a reason. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete Drink → cover → rotate sequence

**Setup:** You are Poisoner, actually CU. Another Coven member has the book. #4 is an eligible nonally; Coven has no plan requiring #4 to act. There is no known dangerous visitor bait. These are example facts, not facts the site knows about a live match.

1. **N1 mode:** Choose ordinary Drink on #4 for a simple disruption plan. If no enemy role is known, choose an eligible unknown nonally; the choice is not a prediction that they must be a TI or killer. Check team plans first.
2. **Private record:** Write `N1: Drink 4 — [actual feedback]`. If interrupted, keep that outcome. Do not fill “success” just because you pressed the ability.
3. **Public cover:** Select **Tavern Keeper — TS** from the unrestricted claim selector. This is logical because the target can genuinely experience a roleblock, which the cover can produce. If a full claim is requested, a compatible deliberately authored public history is `Tavern Keeper / N1: Drink 4`. Do not copy the private Poisoner heading or faction information.
4. **D2 interpretation:** If #4 reports being roleblocked, that supports the action account; it does not prove you are Tavern Keeper or Town. If they report a different effect, do not silently alter your own private action record to fit them.
5. **N2 after successful Drink:** #4 is Hungover. Choose a different useful eligible target, such as an independently identified enemy night actor. Do not promise to roleblock #4 on consecutive nights.
6. **Alternative mode:** Smog blocks incoming visits to the selected house with an obstacle effect; it does not simply stop the owner’s action. Coordinate because allied visits can also be obstructed. Socialite — TS becomes an explainable but difficult alternative, with guest-list and immunity differences. Keeping Tavern Keeper while claiming every Smog report was a roleblock creates a mismatch.
7. **Book branch:** If you receive the book, the direct attack also roleblocks. Do not plan a normal book attack plus Smog together. A dead target and a genuine roleblock effect can change how well the old cover survives.

**What the beginner can now answer:** Which button starts the simple plan? Drink. Who is a legal fallback? A nonally, after checking team interference and visiting danger. What alignment goes public? TS for the Tavern Keeper cover, not actual CU. Who next? A new eligible target after successful Drink. Is Smog the same effect? No.

**Why this cover has a reason:** It matches target feedback as well as an ordinary visit. **Why it is not guaranteed:** A real effect does not establish faction; mode changes, Hangover, the book, and independent observations can expose differences. Cleric remains selectable as TP, but supplies a weaker story because you do not actually Barrier and the target may report disruption.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Privately record Drink/Smog/book attack, target, and actual feedback. A failed action stays failed. A target later saying “roleblocked” can support a Drink story, but silence does not prove your action succeeded.

**What this does and does not establish:** A target reporting roleblock can support your cover; it does not make you Town. A Smog report is not a normal roleblock.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
After a successful Drink, choose a different eligible target because of Hungover. Use D2 evidence to find a useful disruption. If choosing Smog, coordinate access and reconsider the cover; with the book, the attack also roleblocks but does not normally combine with Smog.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Choose a valuable Drink target and a consistent cover.
- **Middle:** Use Smog only when blocking access is better than direct disruption.
- **Late:** Account for book constraints and whether your prior cover still explains tonight’s action.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not use outdated delayed-poison advice. Do not conflate Drink with Smog. Do not claim a roleblock lock through Hangover.

**Important interaction:** Real Socialites and Spies can expose Smog-based stories. Some Coven astral interactions differ from ordinary astral bypass.

**Worked decision:** N1 Drink #4 supports a Tavern Keeper will; choosing Smog N2 means the story must account for a different effect.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Illumination restricts Ritualist. Changing potion mode can undermine a protection cover if a claimed target dies.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: Revealing a role does not reveal all its actions or crimes. A Seer story still lacks the usual two-visit pattern.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not assume you can heal, reveal, and attack simultaneously. Do not give a claim feedback you did not receive. Do not promise immediate Ritualist synergy.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Cleric naturally fits nights actually using Barrier. Sheriff or Investigator can use role knowledge only as an information-fit cover; exact-role knowledge is not their actual result.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Reveal useful unknowns or save an ally when the threat is concrete.
- **Middle:** Use information for team targeting while choosing a sustainable potion-based cover.
- **Late:** Do not lose a necessary kill by assuming Barrier, Reveal, and Harmful all happen together.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: If you genuinely barrier #4, a Cleric-style action matches; if you reveal #7, do not automatically log a proven Murder result.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Choose one legal potion mode for the team’s immediate need: Barrier an ally, Reveal an enemy, or the available book-linked harmful action.

**How to choose:** With no specific threat, coordinated Reveal of an unresolved nonally can supply useful role knowledge. With a threatened ally, Barrier may be better. Do not promise all modes in one night or treat a reveal as a two-person Seer comparison.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose one useful potion mode. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record mode, target, and literal feedback privately. A revealed role is special information, not a Sheriff result, and Illumination can restrict a later Ritualist plan.

**What this does and does not establish:** Revealing a role does not reveal all its actions or crimes. A Seer story still lacks the usual two-visit pattern.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Use the new role knowledge to coordinate a legal team plan, including Ritualist eligibility. Choose the next mode for the current need, and adjust a protective cover if switching to an action with different consequences.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Reveal useful unknowns or save an ally when the threat is concrete.
- **Middle:** Use information for team targeting while choosing a sustainable potion-based cover.
- **Late:** Do not lose a necessary kill by assuming Barrier, Reveal, and Harmful all happen together.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not assume you can heal, reveal, and attack simultaneously. Do not give a claim feedback you did not receive. Do not promise immediate Ritualist synergy.

**Important interaction:** Illumination restricts Ritualist. Changing potion mode can undermine a protection cover if a claimed target dies.

**Worked decision:** If you genuinely barrier #4, a Cleric-style action matches; if you reveal #7, do not automatically log a proven Murder result.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

playbook.headline: My default N1: Silence; Blind a known investigator instead.
playbook.firstNight: With little role information, Silence a nonally likely to contribute to D2 discussion. If you already have a credible investigative target, prefer Blind to deny that night’s results.
playbook.reason: Silence has broad value before you know roles: it removes a speaker’s next-day contribution and restricts vote changes. Blind has greater targeted information-denial value once you know who receives useful results.

For the simplest cover I prefer Cleric (TP) over Psychic (TI): it requires fewer invented results and less daily posting. Neither reproduces your distinctive disruption or supplies genuine protection.
