sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with Coven by eliminating opposing factions; protecting the faction’s path can matter more than personal survival.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Day communication effects and night blindness differ. Voice-mode behavior must not leak into the text guide.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: Missing feedback is different from an ability failing. A victim’s silence is not evidence they voluntarily refused to claim.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not select the same player consecutively via different dolls. Do not interpret silence as inactivity. Do not claim to know information your cover cannot get.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Visiting fallback covers require care because victims receive distinctive disruption. Do not treat Blind as equivalent to ordinary roleblocking.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Disrupt information useful to the next vote.
- **Middle:** Rotate legal targets and coordinate effect timing.
- **Late:** Consider which surviving speaker, reader, or investigator can actually change the outcome.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: Blind an informative opponent: consider whether the benefit outweighs a Tracker correlating your visit with their missing results.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Choose Silence, Deafen, or Blind for one useful nonally. Each interferes with a different part of communication or information.

**How to choose:** Prefer a player whose contribution that mode would disrupt: a public reporter for Silence, for example. With no role evidence, choose an eligible nonally and keep the mode’s limits in mind; Blind is not a roleblock.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose the intended disruption. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the selected mode, target, and actual feedback. A target’s missing message does not prove faction or guarantee that every part of their action stopped.

**What this does and does not establish:** Missing feedback is different from an ability failing. A victim’s silence is not evidence they voluntarily refused to claim.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Choose a different target because changing modes does not bypass the consecutive-player restriction. Use D2 behavior to select a mode with a concrete purpose, and recheck the book action.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Disrupt information useful to the next vote.
- **Middle:** Rotate legal targets and coordinate effect timing.
- **Late:** Consider which surviving speaker, reader, or investigator can actually change the outcome.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not select the same player consecutively via different dolls. Do not interpret silence as inactivity. Do not claim to know information your cover cannot get.

**Important interaction:** Day communication effects and night blindness differ. Voice-mode behavior must not leak into the text guide.

**Worked decision:** Blind an informative opponent: consider whether the benefit outweighs a Tracker correlating your visit with their missing results.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Choose one coherent cover and record the matching subset of Sense.
- **Middle:** Use traffic and whisper knowledge for team decisions without leaking extra information.
- **Late:** Anticipate book acquisition and preserve an explanation for both the result and any attack.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Sense one eligible nonally to learn the available movement information. Keep destinations, visitors, and whisper information separate.

**How to choose:** Prefer a player whose movement could support a useful cover or reveal an important enemy action. With no D1 lead, choose an eligible unknown nonally outside obvious visitor traps.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Capture separate information channels. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record each channel exactly: where the target went, who visited them, and separately any overheard whispers. A missing channel is not a fabricated “no visit.”

**What this does and does not establish:** Knowing both directions is broader than either cover. Whispers can inform choices but are not evidence a Tracker would mechanically receive.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Use D2 claims to Sense someone whose movement can answer a question. If the book arrives, the selected target is also attacked; reassess a cover that depends on them surviving and confirming your account.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Choose one coherent cover and record the matching subset of Sense.
- **Middle:** Use traffic and whisper knowledge for team decisions without leaking extra information.
- **Late:** Anticipate book acquisition and preserve an explanation for both the result and any attack.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

cards.compact: Oracle (TP): conditional fit without book; Cleric (TP): visiting fallback with book. All roles remain selectable.

**Oracle — TP (Town Protective); Conditional fit without book.** No ordinary role action can fit a nonvisible-visit story. **What can expose it:** You do not protect a role, and holding the book changes the movement.

Feed Bread to one eligible other player. Your first milestone is one living recipient, not a kill or a public claim that you protected them.

**How to choose:** Prefer someone likely to survive several cycles. Avoid an obvious imminent execution, a planned victim you know about, or obvious visitor bait. With no useful information, choose an eligible unpressured player and accept that survival is uncertain.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Keep one other recipient alive. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete living-recipient plan

**Setup:** You are a normal-profile solo Baker, actually NA. #4 is eligible, unpressured, not already fed, and not obvious visitor bait. You do not have confirmed knowledge of their role. Other Apocalypse teammates must not be invented; the default bucket is mutually exclusive unless the setup changes it.

1. **N1:** Feed #4. If no player stands out, an eligible unpressured unknown is a workable starting choice. The reason is retaining a living recipient, not proving their faction or granting protection.
2. **Private dawn log:** If the Feed applied and #4 is alive, write `N1: Feed 4; living other recipients: 1`. If blocked, do not add progress. If #4 died, do not keep them in the living count. Your own starting Bread is not an additional other recipient.
3. **Public cover:** If you choose Cleric from the all-role selector, the public alignment is **TP**, while your actual alignment remains NA. A deliberately fabricated cover history can say `Cleric / N1: Barrier 4`; the private truth remains Feed. This is a role-deception example for the game, not a real Barrier result. The site must never generate a saved-player message from Bread or leak the private progress counter into the public will.
4. **D2 target planning:** Read claims and pressure. A player about to be executed is a poor new Feed candidate if another likely survivor exists. A highly exposed player expected to be killed can also lose your progress. Do not fight every case solely because your recipient is involved; that can expose your priorities.
5. **N2, recipient alive:** Feed a different eligible likely survivor, say #7. If both applied recipients remain alive at the next dawn, your ordinary other-recipient count is two.
6. **N2, recipient dead or failed:** Your count is lower; choose a replacement or a fresh eligible recipient. Refeeding an already fed living player does not add another recipient. A later third living other recipient reaches the ordinary threshold; reduced-population rules can change it, so follow actual transformation feedback.

details.markdown:
Feed Bread to one eligible other player. Your first milestone is one living recipient, not a kill or a public claim that you protected them.

**How to choose:** Prefer someone likely to survive several cycles. Avoid an obvious imminent execution, a planned victim you know about, or obvious visitor bait. With no useful information, choose an eligible unpressured player and accept that survival is uncertain.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Keep one other recipient alive. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

### A concrete living-recipient plan

**Setup:** You are a normal-profile solo Baker, actually NA. #4 is eligible, unpressured, not already fed, and not obvious visitor bait. You do not have confirmed knowledge of their role. Other Apocalypse teammates must not be invented; the default bucket is mutually exclusive unless the setup changes it.

1. **N1:** Feed #4. If no player stands out, an eligible unpressured unknown is a workable starting choice. The reason is retaining a living recipient, not proving their faction or granting protection.
2. **Private dawn log:** If the Feed applied and #4 is alive, write `N1: Feed 4; living other recipients: 1`. If blocked, do not add progress. If #4 died, do not keep them in the living count. Your own starting Bread is not an additional other recipient.
3. **Public cover:** If you choose Cleric from the all-role selector, the public alignment is **TP**, while your actual alignment remains NA. A deliberately fabricated cover history can say `Cleric / N1: Barrier 4`; the private truth remains Feed. This is a role-deception example for the game, not a real Barrier result. The site must never generate a saved-player message from Bread or leak the private progress counter into the public will.
4. **D2 target planning:** Read claims and pressure. A player about to be executed is a poor new Feed candidate if another likely survivor exists. A highly exposed player expected to be killed can also lose your progress. Do not fight every case solely because your recipient is involved; that can expose your priorities.
5. **N2, recipient alive:** Feed a different eligible likely survivor, say #7. If both applied recipients remain alive at the next dawn, your ordinary other-recipient count is two.
6. **N2, recipient dead or failed:** Your count is lower; choose a replacement or a fresh eligible recipient. Refeeding an already fed living player does not add another recipient. A later third living other recipient reaches the ordinary threshold; reduced-population rules can change it, so follow actual transformation feedback.
7. **After Famine:** Stop using the pre-transform Feed plan. Work on remaining bread-holders with Starve and survive the day vote. The public transformation announcement does not itself name you, but it changes the lobby’s priorities. Invincible Defense does not prevent hanging.

sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: Infect players; contact spreads infection and provides propagation information. Adjacent neighbors begin infected in the current baseline. Infect all living opponents to become Pestilence.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with the Apocalypse faction by eliminating its opponents. Transformation advances your power; it is not itself the final win condition.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Astral contact does not spread infection normally. Solo/multi-member Apocalypse changes detection and defense.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: Already infected players do not create a fresh infection event for every visit. Infection history is broader and less direct than a clean observer log.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not count starting neighbor infections as N1 visitors. Do not assert every missing infection means no visit. Do not publish unobserved destinations.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Tracker/Lookout are conditional information fits. Infections can support parts of those stories but are not automatically exhaustive or equivalent every night.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Separate seeded infections from useful new spread.
- **Middle:** Target remaining uninfected opponents and use propagation carefully.
- **Late:** After Pestilence, manage stack-based pressure and the day vote rather than pretending it is a conventional rampage.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: #4 becomes newly infected through contact: identify what the actual feedback establishes before writing a numbered Tracker result.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Check the seeded infections, then Infect an eligible player not already infected. Seeded neighbors are not players you visited on N1.

**How to choose:** Prefer a likely active visitor or well-connected house that can spread infection. With no D1 evidence, choose an eligible uninfected unknown outside obvious visitor bait; there is no guaranteed optimal target.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Expand beyond seeded infections. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Privately separate initial infections, your chosen Infect, and later spread. Spread can suggest contact but is not a complete Lookout report with guaranteed visitor identities.

**What this does and does not establish:** Already infected players do not create a fresh infection event for every visit. Infection history is broader and less direct than a clean observer log.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Infect a new eligible uninfected player after updating the map from actual feedback. If transformation occurs, read Pestilence’s current stack/death rules rather than using old automatic-rampage advice.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Separate seeded infections from useful new spread.
- **Middle:** Target remaining uninfected opponents and use propagation carefully.
- **Late:** After Pestilence, manage stack-based pressure and the day vote rather than pretending it is a conventional rampage.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

**After transformation:** Pestilence: infection becomes stack-based danger; reaching three stacks is lethal while the effect is active. Its own spread action can force maximum stacks and is not a conventional harmful attack. Do not use the old ToS1 passive-rampage model.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not count starting neighbor infections as N1 visitors. Do not assert every missing infection means no visit. Do not publish unobserved destinations.

**Important interaction:** Astral contact does not spread infection normally. Solo/multi-member Apocalypse changes detection and defense.

**Worked decision:** #4 becomes newly infected through contact: identify what the actual feedback establishes before writing a numbered Tracker result.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

**How priorities change:**

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Oracle (TP): astral movement fit; Sheriff (TI): information story; weak movement fit. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Oracle — TP (Town Protective); Astral movement fit.** Reap and Aegis do not require an ordinary numbered visible visit. **What can expose it:** You supply no protection and must claim role-based Aegis choices, not Reap targets.

**Sheriff — TI (Town Investigative); Information story; weak movement fit.** Reap’s framing effect can align with some suspicious-looking evidence. **What can expose it:** A real Sheriff normally visits; your astral Reap does not reproduce that, and you receive no genuine check.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

cards.title: Mistakes and important interactions
cards.compact: Do not use a normal visiting cover without acknowledging the risk. Do not assume Reap itself kills. Do not miss the day urgency after transformation.
cards.expanded:
Do not use a normal visiting cover without acknowledging the risk. Do not assume Reap itself kills. Do not miss the day urgency after transformation.

**Important interaction:** Reap can override other apparent-faction effects. Source prose differs on some faction nuances; default advice is explicitly normal Apocalypse.

**Worked decision:** A prominent player is likely to die tonight: reaping them can advance progress, while your public will must not reveal private soul knowledge.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with the Apocalypse faction by eliminating its opponents. Transformation advances your power; it is not itself the final win condition.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Reap likely deaths without breaking a no-visit story.
- **Middle:** Track passive and extra souls and prepare for transformation visibility.
- **Late:** After Death, survival through the day is the urgent objective.

sections.title: Worked decision
sections.markdown: A prominent player is likely to die tonight: reaping them can advance progress, while your public will must not reveal private soul knowledge.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Reap one eligible player whose death might add to your soul progress. Reap is astral; you are not making an ordinary visible visit.

**How to choose:** Prefer someone plausibly at risk of death rather than a likely long-term survivor. With no evidence, choose a legal unknown and rely on the ordinary passive soul progression rather than pretending to predict the night kill.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Track passive and extra souls separately. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the real soul total, passive gain, and any extra gain from a reaped death. Do not count every dead player as a successfully reaped target.

**What this does and does not establish:** A target appearing suspicious does not expose their actual role. Your framing cannot be treated as a genuine Town check.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Choose the next plausible death target using D2 cases and threats. Use the actual total rather than an assumed schedule. If you become Death, prioritize surviving the required day instead of continuing ordinary Reap instructions.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Reap likely deaths without breaking a no-visit story.
- **Middle:** Track passive and extra souls and prepare for transformation visibility.
- **Late:** After Death, survival through the day is the urgent objective.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

**After transformation:** Death: survive the day after the public transformation so the end-of-day Apocalypse can occur. Vote pressure, not ordinary night defense, becomes the central threat. Keep private soul counts out of a cover will.

sections.title: Win condition

Successfully confirm the required three-player guess set. The later deaths are a consequence, not a separate victory requirement.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Collect claims; no N1 confirmed guess.
- **Middle:** Build supported three-player sets and confirm them.
- **Late:** Do not wait until too few targets remain; failed feedback does not identify the wrong member.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
You cannot confirm the three-role doom on N1. Collect role claims and keep guesses private instead of inventing a first-night success.

**How to choose:** No confirmed N1 doom target set is needed. Note exact claims that may later be eligible; TI is excluded. Do not treat disputed Neutral Outlier eligibility as settled immunity.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Collect exact eligible role evidence. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Separate public claims from role knowledge you actually possess. A confident claim may be false, so a three-person guess set needs more than three names.

**What this does and does not establish:** At least one wrong guess does not reveal which one failed. Correct-looking claims can be deceptive.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
When confirmation is enabled, enter and confirm all three eligible target/guess pairs only when the evidence justifies the attempt. If a guess is uncertain, improve the information instead of presenting the set as known.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Collect claims; no N1 confirmed guess.
- **Middle:** Build supported three-player sets and confirm them.
- **Late:** Do not wait until too few targets remain; failed feedback does not identify the wrong member.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Sheriff (TI): pressure story; weak movement fit; Oracle (TP): nonvisit fallback. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Sheriff — TI (Town Investigative); Pressure story; weak movement fit.** A claimed suspicious result can create a reason to question the assigned target. **What can expose it:** It is fabricated and you normally did not visit; observers, framing context, and overfocusing can expose it.

**Oracle — TP (Town Protective); Nonvisit fallback.** No normal night action can fit the cover’s astral footprint. **What can expose it:** It supplies no real protection and does not by itself motivate your target’s execution.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

If enabled, choose an eligible nonally to attack and deliberately check Cautious mode. Grace Period can prevent an opening kill.

**How to choose:** Prefer a useful enemy with no obvious defense or visitor trap. With no evidence, choose an eligible unknown; a random legal attack is not an exact role test. Cautious changes retaliation behavior, so do not leave the toggle unexplained.

sections.title: Role and ability
sections.markdown: Attack directly or Shroud another player so their direct visits carry attacks. If they do not directly visit, the fallback attacks that target; visibility has documented inconsistencies.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Eliminate opposing factions until only your allied Shroud faction remains.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Shroud can make friendly visitors harmful to guards/traps and affect Investigator/Coroner interpretation.

sections.title: Read the information
sections.markdown: A death can reveal something about a Shrouded player’s destination, but not all movement when nobody dies or multiple visits occur.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not promise invisibility in every fallback. Do not claim exhaustive visit information. Do not assume the attacked-looking Town visitor acted voluntarily.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Oracle may fit successful astral Shrouding; Tracker is only a narrow inferred-information story, not a full observer equivalent.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Use a plausible visiting target to carry the attack.
- **Middle:** Separate inferred destinations from exhaustive tracking claims.
- **Late:** Account for direct fallback and choose a kill route that also leaves a viable day explanation.

sections.markdown: Shroud #4 and #9 dies: that may support a destination inference, but a complete fabricated Tracker history still requires more information.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Choose direct Attack or Shroud for a concrete reason. Shrouding a player and directly attacking them are different plans.

**How to choose:** A likely active visitor may carry a useful Shroud attack; direct Attack is easier to understand when you want the selected player as the victim. With no role evidence, do not assume a random target will visit the house you want.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Choose mode for a specific victim plan. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the selected mode and actual outcomes. If the carrier did not visit, fallback and visibility details are conditional; do not invent a full destination report from the deaths.

**What this does and does not establish:** A death can reveal something about a Shrouded player’s destination, but not all movement when nobody dies or multiple visits occur.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Use D2 claims to choose a more useful carrier or a direct victim. Preserve uncertainty for disputed visibility/fallback interactions instead of basing the entire cover on an untested rule.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Use a plausible visiting target to carry the attack.
- **Middle:** Separate inferred destinations from exhaustive tracking claims.
- **Late:** Account for direct fallback and choose a kill route that also leaves a viable day explanation.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not promise invisibility in every fallback. Do not claim exhaustive visit information. Do not assume the attacked-looking Town visitor acted voluntarily.

**Important interaction:** Shroud can make friendly visitors harmful to guards/traps and affect Investigator/Coroner interpretation.

**Worked decision:** Shroud #4 and #9 dies: that may support a destination inference, but a complete fabricated Tracker history still requires more information.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

cards.title: Claim choices and logical fit
cards.compact: Tracker (TI): real information; conditional movement; Cleric (TP): visiting fallback on attacks. All roles remain selectable.
cards.expanded:
**Tracker — TI (Town Investigative); Real information; conditional movement.** Persistent Scent supplies real movement information. **What can expose it:** On later attack nights you may visibly go elsewhere; information fit does not fix personal movement.

**Cleric — TP (Town Protective); Visiting fallback on attacks.** A chosen attack house can share a claimed Barrier destination. **What can expose it:** No real protection exists; rampage and kill details differ.

These are starting explanations, not a whitelist. Choose any role from the full roster, including a weak fit, and read that claim’s real obligations inline. Matching one visible visit is weaker than matching movement, result scope, target feedback, and later demonstration together. Keep actual actions private and deliberately author the public cover; do not treat invented cover text as a genuine game result.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Eliminate opposing factions until only your allied Werewolf faction remains.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

sections.title: Interactions and limits
sections.markdown: Jail, roleblock, and Control have dangerous retaliation/redirection interactions. Use the actual Full Moon indicator rather than an unverified schedule.

sections.title: Read the information

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.markdown: Do not invent new scent targets on every night. Do not assume roleblock simply disables Full Moon danger. Do not call the Tracker cover universally strong.

sections.title: Claim timing and disclosure
sections.markdown: Tracker is an information fit only when the reported target actually has scent coverage. Your visible attack destination may contradict the claimed tracking target.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Acquire useful scent coverage on eligible nights.
- **Middle:** Choose rampages without pretending persistent results are fresh personal visits.
- **Late:** Use the actual moon/action state and preserve a credible voting position.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Check the actual Full Moon indicator. On a non-Full-Moon opening, choose a Scent target rather than inventing an unavailable attack.

**How to choose:** Scent a likely active eligible nonally whose later movement could be useful. With no D1 lead, choose an unknown outside obvious visiting traps. If the setup actually permits an attack, assess the rampage and visitor risk first.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Follow the actual moon state. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the Scent target and its continuing information separately from your own destination. An old target’s later movement does not mean you personally visited them again.

**What this does and does not establish:** Persistent information does not imply a fresh visit to that player. Attacking one house while reporting another player’s movement creates observer risk.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Follow the client’s current moon state. If attacking, choose a useful victim and account for rampage traffic; if scenting, update the information plan. Keep persistent Scent reports separate from tonight’s attack.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Acquire useful scent coverage on eligible nights.
- **Middle:** Choose rampages without pretending persistent results are fresh personal visits.
- **Late:** Use the actual moon/action state and preserve a credible voting position.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not invent new scent targets on every night. Do not assume roleblock simply disables Full Moon danger. Do not call the Tracker cover universally strong.

**Important interaction:** Jail, roleblock, and Control have dangerous retaliation/redirection interactions. Use the actual Full Moon indicator rather than an unverified schedule.

**Worked decision:** You marked #4 earlier but attack #9 tonight: a Tracker story about #4 can be informationally true while failing a check of your own movement.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Win condition

For default Wandering Souls, eliminate every Cursed Soul role while at least one faction member remains alive. Acquiring another role does not replace your faction objective.

sections.title: Early, middle, and late game
sections.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Track the first actual swap and retain faction identity.
- **Middle:** Use acquired abilities toward eliminating Cursed Souls.
- **Late:** Count which Cursed Soul roles remain and whether a faction member will survive the final elimination.

details.title: Actions, targeting and opening restrictions
details.markdown:
Prepare for the mandatory astral role swap. Select a desired legal target, but expect the actual acquired role to differ under the swap rules.

**How to choose:** Choose a role opportunity using real claims if available. With no evidence, choose a legal unknown and keep an open plan. Town/Wandering Souls swap randomness means intention is not a guaranteed destination.

**Your opening checkpoint:** Observe the actual swap result. You do not need a perfect read of the lobby to begin; you need a legal action or a deliberate hold and an honest record of what happened.

details.title: Feedback and evidence
details.markdown:
Record the actual acquired role and unchanged faction, not just the player you selected. Open the new role’s instructions while retaining the previous role history.

**What this does and does not establish:** Knowing an old role does not establish a player’s current role. Role-swapped Town abilities need not belong to Town faction.

Keep intended action, actual feedback, and your interpretation in separate sentences. “No result” must not silently become a negative result, a successful save, or confirmation of another player’s faction.

details.title: Progression and later actions
details.markdown:
Follow the role you actually acquired and its current legal controls. If another swap is relevant, preserve history again; do not reset charges/progress by assumption where the interaction is uncertain.

**How priorities change:**

- **Early:** Track the first actual swap and retain faction identity.
- **Middle:** Use acquired abilities toward eliminating Cursed Souls.
- **Late:** Count which Cursed Soul roles remain and whether a faction member will survive the final elimination.

Reassess from the actual outcome, not from the outcome you hoped for. If you are redirected, converted, retrained, or transformed, keep the previous action history and switch to the current legal role/state instructions.

details.title: Exceptions and pitfalls
details.markdown:
Do not use old age/youngest-biter rules. Do not assume converting any defended or non-Town player succeeds. Do not assume a dead Vampire means the faction is gone.

**Important interaction:** Converted teammates can inherit Vampire after its death. The page flags a solo-detection bug; do not promise innocence as guaranteed.

**Worked decision:** A previously demonstrated role is converted: keep its mechanical proof while changing its allegiance in private faction notes.

A counterexample is a reason to narrow your conclusion. If an unresolved interaction matters to this decision, use the source note and the actual client feedback rather than turning it into a hard clearance or accusation.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with the Apocalypse faction by eliminating its opponents. Transformation advances your power; it is not itself the final win condition.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Role and ability
details.markdown: Feed Bread to three other living players to become Famine, with a reduced-population exception. Bread recipients need to survive; you already possess Bread.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Win condition
details.markdown:
Win with the Apocalypse faction by eliminating its opponents. Transformation advances your power; it is not itself the final win condition.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Interactions and limits
details.markdown: Bodyguard/Trap do not ordinarily respond to a nonharmful Feed. Blocks and obstacles can delay progress.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Read the information
details.markdown: Transformation is public evidence that a threshold was met, not public identification of which player transformed.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Common mistakes
details.markdown: Do not count your starting Bread as an ordinary recipient. Do not assume dead recipients count. Do not reveal an evil role as a beginner survival tactic.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Claim timing and disclosure
details.markdown: A quiet visiting cover such as Psychic or Cleric can fit pre-transformation movement but supplies no genuine investigative/protection result.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Early, middle, and late game
details.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Feed likely survivors.
- **Middle:** Protect progress from recipient deaths without exposing the goal.
- **Late:** After Famine, focus on bread-holders and survival through the vote rather than further Feed actions.

details.title: Baker before transformation · Worked decision
details.markdown: If #4 is likely to be eliminated tomorrow, feeding a less threatened eligible player can retain progress.

playbook.headline: Default as War: Select two different opposing houses.
playbook.firstNight: You are already transformed: confirm two distinct useful opponents for your Unstoppable rampages. Do not revert to the Berserker one-target buildup plan.
playbook.reason: Two selected houses can remove two residents plus visitors. Omitting the second target gives up a major part of your current power, while Invincible Defense makes daytime identification and hanging the main ordinary danger.
playbook.targetRule: Prioritize opponents who can organize your execution or provide decisive votes. If their threat is similar, favor houses likely to attract other opponents. Exclude actual allies if your setup contains them.
playbook.pivot: If one intended target dies or is no longer eligible before selection, replace them. Against another Invincible opponent, do not assume Unstoppable damage guarantees the kill; recalculate the endgame.
laterPriorities: Survive daytime voting while keeping your cover consistent with known movement.
Confirm both separate targets every night to remove the most dangerous opposing voters.
Use visitor traffic to increase rampage value after selecting the essential threats.
playbook.expanded: War has its own current-state rules, including bypassing common disruption; reread your actual card instead of assuming Berserker restrictions persist. Coroner and Trapper offer alternative inactive openings, while Deputy is short but easily tested. No Town cover reproduces growing attacks and Rampage indefinitely. After becoming War, a two-house Unstoppable Rampage no longer resembles a normal Vigilante shot or single-person protection visit. You are War now: a pre-transformation cover does not explain new attacks, altered movement, or the public transformation.

options.why: Your normal N1 inactivity resembles Vigilante loading before a later shot, so you can avoid inventing an opening visit.
options.exposure: Berserker kills are not Vigilante shots. Attack upgrades, Rampage, death attribution and the load/ammunition sequence can expose the difference.
strategy: Write N1: Load as the cover, while privately recording that Berserker had no legal N1 attack.
From N2, a claimed shot must fit an actual prior Load; you cannot report a shot every night as though Vigilante has endless ready ammunition.

strategy: Write Aegis Sheriff or another legal Town role, not Aegis 4. The private Reap target and public role choice are different kinds of selection.
Rotate the claimed role on consecutive nights and keep the Oracle self-role choice to its one permitted use.
Do not call a marked player saved or identified. Reap adds a Soul opportunity and changes apparent investigation identity; it is not a Barrier.

options.bestWhen: You want a quieter cover that does not promise a visible visit every night.

options.why: Reap can make a marked player appear Suspicious, so some other Sheriff evidence may align with a pressure story rather than contradicting it immediately.
options.exposure: You receive no Sheriff check and do not make its normal visible visit. Repeated Suspicious reports on your marked players can reveal the framing plan.
strategy: Use only legal Innocent/Suspicious vocabulary and post a stable cover check promptly; a Reap selection is not itself a result.
Expect a Tracker or Lookout to challenge the missing normal visit to your alleged Search target.

options.bestWhen: Public investigative evidence already supports questioning a marked player, and you understand that the apparent result is not their true faction.

options.why: Astral Reap leaves no ordinary visit, which fits a stay-at-home Veteran account better than claiming to walk to a house every night.
options.exposure: You cannot produce Alert attacks or a valid visitor-kill event. An unharmed confirmed direct visitor during a claimed Alert can expose the missing effect.
strategy: Separate the private Reap target from the public home-based ability: Veteran does not Alert at another player’s house.
Keep an accurate claimed three-charge Alert count and do not write Alert automatically on every night.
Do not invent kills or visitor identities from Souls gained; a marked player can die elsewhere with no connection to your house.
A quiet stay-home account is possible but weak. If real direct visitors report surviving an Alert, the movement fit cannot repair the missing attack.
After becoming Death, reassess this earlier cover against your new ability and any public transformation; do not claim the old movement pattern automatically continues.
options.bestWhen: You want a nonvisiting TK cover and have no public event requiring a real Alert demonstration.

options.why: The ordinary Coroner has no usable N1 autopsy, giving a plausible inactive opening without pretending Reap is a visible visit.
options.exposure: Later Coroner Examine normally requires movement and actual corpse records, neither of which Reap supplies.
strategy: Start with no usable N1 Autopsy; never name a killer comparison before an eligible body exists.
Record a real eligible daytime corpse before alleging the corresponding night Examine.
Do not turn the death of a marked player into a killer match. Soul gain tells you about your objective, not Coroner evidence.
Expect later movement checks to expose the missing Examine visit; the inactive first night is a limited overlap, not a full-role imitation.
After becoming Death, reassess this earlier cover against your new ability and any public transformation; do not claim the old movement pattern automatically continues.
options.bestWhen: You need a plausible N1 and are willing to manage a much weaker later TI history.

options.why: A setup-legal Pilgrim expects no active night visit or result, fitting astral Reap’s observed inactivity without promising an effect you cannot demonstrate.
options.exposure: Pilgrim must be possible in the deck. A bare no-ability claim supplies little trust and can become a convenient execution target.
strategy: Check roledeck eligibility before selecting this claim; common Town buckets do not automatically permit every Outlier.
Use dated public observations and vote reasons rather than pretending Soul counts are Town information.
Do not add a night target or special result to make the will look busier; Pilgrim has no such ability.
When Death appears, your public reasoning needs to stand on its own because the cover cannot independently confirm you.
After becoming Death, reassess this earlier cover against your new ability and any public transformation; do not claim the old movement pattern automatically continues.
options.bestWhen: The roledeck explicitly allows Town Outliers and you prefer an observation-based account to fabricated powers.

routes.label: Survive the transformation day
routes.headline: Default as Death: Survive today; there is no next-night buildup.
routes.when: As Death, the transformation day is the decisive phase: survive it with a stable account and checkable answers.
routes.action: Your immediate decision is daytime survival. Keep a consistent claim, answer accusations with checkable facts and avoid supplying a fresh contradiction that makes you the easy hanging.
routes.targetRule: Focus your attention on the players organizing votes against you. With no accusation yet, participate plausibly and preserve your cover instead of volunteering the transformed identity.
routes.reason: The Apocalypse resolves at sundown if you survive the day. Another Reap target or extra Soul no longer improves that win condition; staying off the final execution is the entire urgent objective.
routes.pivot: When nominated, address the strongest specific evidence against you before arguing broad possibilities. If actual allies exist in the setup, coordinate legal voting support; normal Apocalypse usually has no teammates.
goals: Prevent your own execution during the transformation day.
Answer the strongest accusation without contradicting your recorded claim or movement.
Remain in the match and reach sundown alive so the automatic Apocalypse can resolve.

routes.label: Answer the strongest case directly
routes.when: One concrete contradiction or competing account is concentrating votes on you.
routes.action: Identify the exact accusation, give the shortest consistent timeline that addresses it, and point to facts the lobby can check now. Preserve your previous claim rather than inventing a new night ability.
routes.targetRule: Your target is the decisive public objection, not a player to Reap. Compare your existing movement and claim history with the accusation.
routes.reason: Fixing one checkable misunderstanding can cost the opposing majority its strongest reason to execute you. Adding several unsupported stories increases the chance of a new contradiction.
routes.pivot: If the evidence truly exposes you, assess the actual vote coalition and any other supported urgent case; do not promise another night result that Death cannot produce.
laterPriorities: Track nominations and remaining opposing votes during this day.
Use discussion to preserve survival rather than to plan Reap.
Remain in the game through the end-of-day resolution.
routes.risk: A sound explanation may still fail against a coordinated majority. The transformation announcement makes Town especially likely to compare every claim.

sections.title: Current ability and objective
sections.markdown: Death: survive the day after the public transformation so the end-of-day Apocalypse can occur. Vote pressure, not ordinary night defense, becomes the central threat. Keep private soul counts out of a cover will.

sections.title: What to do now
sections.markdown: Death has no useful night action to queue. Invincible Defense does not make a hanging safe, and quitting does not deliver Armageddon. This replaces Soul Collector’s plan immediately after transformation. Deception can buy the day; fabricated results remain invented.

sections.title: Transition and cover limits
sections.markdown: Oracle matches astral Reap’s lack of an ordinary visit most cleanly; Sheriff can pressure a genuinely framed appearance but invents a check and a visible visit. Veteran, Coroner and setup-legal Pilgrim are progressively weaker alternatives for the nonvisiting history. Reap never supplies Town investigation or protection. After becoming Death, the only immediate route is surviving the current day. There is no next Reap or ordinary nighttime ability to promise. You are Death now: a pre-transformation cover does not explain new attacks, altered movement, or the public transformation.

sections.title: Win condition
sections.markdown:
Win with the Apocalypse faction by eliminating its opponents. Transformation advances your power; it is not itself the final win condition.

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Role and ability
details.markdown: Astrally Reap players for extra souls when they die, plus passive nightly progress. Reap also frames targets. Seven souls transform you into Death.

details.markdown:

The statement assumes the default faction profile. Conversion or Flexible Factions can change the applicable faction objective. A role swap alone does not change your faction.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Interactions and limits
details.markdown: Reap can override other apparent-faction effects. Source prose differs on some faction nuances; default advice is explicitly normal Apocalypse.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Read the information
details.markdown: A target appearing suspicious does not expose their actual role. Your framing cannot be treated as a genuine Town check.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Common mistakes
details.markdown: Do not use a normal visiting cover without acknowledging the risk. Do not assume Reap itself kills. Do not miss the day urgency after transformation.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Claim timing and disclosure
details.markdown: Oracle is movement-compatible but lacks real protection. Sheriff can align with framing effects only as an information story and conflicts with your astral no-visit pattern.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Early, middle, and late game
details.markdown:
These are recommendations, not forced actions:

- **Early:** Reap likely deaths without breaking a no-visit story.
- **Middle:** Track passive and extra souls and prepare for transformation visibility.
- **Late:** After Death, survival through the day is the urgent objective.

details.title: Soul Collector before transformation · Worked decision
details.markdown: A prominent player is likely to die tonight: reaping them can advance progress, while your public will must not reveal private soul knowledge.

glossary.markdown:
# Beginner glossary and clear communication

These explanations apply to the default vanilla text-chat profile. They are original concise definitions; role-specific exceptions remain in the mechanics chapter. Sources: [alignments](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Alignment_(ToS2)), [keywords](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Keywords_(ToS2)), [attributes](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Attributes_(ToS2)).

| Term | Plain-language meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Role | Your ability set; it can differ from your current faction |
| Faction | The team/win objective you currently belong to |
| Alignment / subalignment | A role family such as Town Protective; chat often calls this alignment |
| Claim | What you tell others your role or category is |
| Full claim | Naming your exact role, usually with the relevant action history |
| Fake claim / cover | A role story different from your actual role |
| Will | A concise record of claimed role, actions, and results |
| N1 / N2 | Night 1 / Night 2; label the night the action occurred |
| D2 / D3 | Day 2 / Day 3; important for day abilities |
| TI | Town Investigative: information-gathering roles |
| TP | Town Protective: roles that protect in distinct ways |
| TK | Town Killing: lethal or attack-handling Town roles; do not abbreviate Tavern Keeper this way in this app |
| TS | Town Support: support abilities that do not fit the other families |
| TPow | Town Power: unique high-impact roles; it is different from TP |
| CPOW / CK / CD / CU | Coven Power / Killing / Deception / Utility |
| NE / NK / NA | Neutral Evil / Neutral Killing / Neutral Apocalypse |
| Outlier | Setup-dependent role that normally needs explicit availability or a suitable modifier |
| VFA | Vote for Alignment: pressure players to state a role category |
| VFR | Vote for Role: pressure players to state an exact role; not identical to VFA |
| TP/LO | A request for protection and Lookout attention; do not blindly send dangerous visitor-attacking roles |
| CC | Counterclaim: a claim competing with another claim for credibility or constrained role space |
| Claim space | The set of role possibilities still compatible with the setup and reliable evidence |
| Unique | Normally at most one instance of that role in the role list; transitions/effects need context |
| 1-for-1 / 1f1 | A claimed conflict where at least one side is wrong under stated assumptions; it does not automatically identify the liar |
| RB | Roleblock: interruption of an eligible ability |
| UO | Unknown Obstacle: destination-related failure, not necessarily a roleblock |
| Astral | Does not behave as an ordinary visit for many observers and visitor hazards |
| Direct visit | A normal visit to a selected destination; visibility is separate from whether it is harmful |
| Harmful visit | An attacking action relevant to specific interception mechanics |
| NV | Often “no visit”; this app prefers “No visible visit” to avoid implying no action |
| Inno / Sus | Innocent / Suspicious appearance to a check; neither is an exact role |
| Barrier / Defense | Protection properties; sufficient defense depends on the attack and special mechanics |
| Rampage | An attack effect that can also strike visitors at the chosen house |
| Book | Necronomicon: changes Coven killing and some role behavior |
| Confirmed | An overloaded chat term: specify whether an ability was demonstrated, a result was observed, or faction was established under current assumptions |
| Push | Present a case and encourage action against a player |
| Flip | A revealed role/faction after death; hidden or altered deaths need caution |
| Majority / parity | Voting-control concepts; count actual weighted votes rather than only living bodies |

## Message structure the beginner cards should teach

Use **observation → limited meaning → useful question**.

- “Sheriff, N1 #4 Innocent. This does not clear them. What are they claiming?”
- “Tracker, N2 #7 -> #9. #7 says they went to #4; was there redirection?”
- “Investigator, N2 #7 Trespassing. Who have they visited? The result alone does not prove evil.”

These are invented examples for learning phrasing, not live results or a recommendation to fabricate Town information. Real players should report the feedback they actually received; an evil maintaining a cover needs to understand the same logical limitations.

sourceSummary.uncertaintiesMarkdown:
# Uncertainty and correction register

Research date: 2026-10-15. The research pass is complete; **some game interactions remain externally uncertain**. A wiki assertion is not a live-client experiment. These entries define what the website can safely say and what it must not turn into an automatic rule.

## Resolved enough to use as the baseline

| ID | Issue found | Decision and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R01 | Wildling has a stale upcoming-change banner and inconsistent history date | Keep text-mode Sense/whisper behavior. Attune is voice-only; use the official July 27, 2026 patch date. [Official](https://www.townofsalem.io/town-of-salem-2-introducing-voice-chat-mode-%F0%9F%93%9C%F0%9F%8E%89%F0%9F%94%8A-patch-notes-r1-5-14/), [role](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Wildling_(ToS2)). |
| R02 | Old guides reverse Psychic nights | Odd Good/two, even Evil/three. Do not import old example wills. [Role](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Psychic_(ToS2)). |
| R03 | Old role name and retraining limits | Search Coven Leader as alias; display Archmage. Use current restriction on retraining other players. [Official](https://www.townofsalem.io/town-of-salem-2-flexible-factions-update-patch-notes-r1-5-11/). |
| R04 | Cursed Soul wiki.gg Swap section is blank, shared keyword incomplete | Use role/faction separation and faction-dependent randomization from secondary role detail and official 2025 changes. Avoid a fully simulated Swap resolver. [Secondary role](https://town-of-salem.fandom.com/wiki/Cursed_Soul), [official announcement](https://steamstore-a.akamaihd.net/news/externalpost/steam_community_announcements/1810503566584385). |
| R05 | Baker prose could mistakenly count its own starting Bread | Use three other living fed players for ordinary progress; own starting Bread is not a recipient action. Preserve the reduced-population exception. [Baker](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Baker_(ToS2)), [secondary](https://town-of-salem.fandom.com/wiki/Baker). |
| R07 | Illusionist strategy still suggests concealment from Bodyguard, Trapper, and Deputy | Use the official R1.5.11 correction: Illusion no longer hides from those interactions. Do not repeat the stale strategy. [Official](https://www.townofsalem.io/town-of-salem-2-flexible-factions-update-patch-notes-r1-5-11/). |
| R06 | Wiki dates differ by a day on several 2025 changes | Official published date is the chronology reference. Preserve actual wiki revision timestamps separately. |

## Keep out of hard deductions and validators

| ID | Dispute / missing evidence | Implementation decision | What would settle it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U01 | wiki.gg Doomsayer says Neutral Outliers cannot be guessed; Fandom says exact-role guesses; official R1.5.13 fixes Vampire/Cursed Soul in the UI | Explain the conflict. Do not tell Outlier players they are certainly immune. Keep a manual guess field; do not derive a hard exclusion from wiki.gg | Current client dropdown and a controlled test of Vampire/Cursed Soul guesses, including flexed cases |
| U02 | Investigator source says executions are excluded, while its strategy later names Jailor as a Murder explanation | Do not automatically add Murder to executions or clear a disputed result; show the actual observed feedback | Current Jailor/Investigator test with no framing or extra attack |
| U03 | Coroner marks some Bodyguard/counterattack and special-killer cases untested | Give ordinary Autopsy/Examine behavior; do not ship an exhaustive killer-interaction truth table | Controlled cases with full action histories |
| U04 | Psychic no-vision paragraphs conflict with its current night parity and contain an outdated warning | Use normal vision format; preserve no-result/manual feedback without predicting the exact late-game message | Current odd/even small-town tests |
| U05 | Serial Killer counterattack is labeled Unstoppable on one page while describing natural Invincible bypass and protection exceptions; keyword page calls it Unstoppable+ | Say it can be exceptionally dangerous and has protective exceptions. Do not reduce it to the ordinary attack/defense comparison | Current controlled retaliation tests against natural and granted defense |
| U06 | Shroud source flags inconsistent direct fallback/astral priority | Label Oracle-style movement compatibility conditional; do not promise guaranteed invisibility | Reproduce visiting, idle, blocked, astral, and jailed target cases |
| U07 | Spy role description is brief about exact trigger exhaustiveness, framed visitors, and multiple concurrent bugs | Store literal role feedback and separate active bugs. Do not infer player identity or a global no-evil-visits clear | Current feedback examples and controlled frame/astral/multi-bug cases |
| U08 | Catalyst has numerous role-dependent day/night effects and known fixed bugs | Explain extra actions next cycle; keep uncommon effect timing advisory/manual rather than a full simulator | Current per-role Overcharge matrix tested against the installed build |
| U09 | Vampire page notes a solo detection-immunity bug | Describe intended solo defense/detection with a visible exception; no guaranteed Sheriff innocence rule | Current reproduction and a confirming fix note |
| U10 | Cursed Soul/admirer progress transfer, successor ties, and unusual custom-faction interactions are inconsistently documented | Preserve actual transitions and feedback; do not recompute hidden progress automatically | Controlled swap/conversion tests with known initial state |
| U11 | Some role strategy claims overstate “proof,” assume old faction rules, or give anecdotal survival claims | Use conditional evidence labels and authored strategic reasoning; never invent percentages | This is a design correction, not a missing fact to guess |
| U12 | Exact game will/chat character limits and clipboard handling were not verified through a live client | Preserve user text and show copyable output. Verify limits before adding enforced truncation | Current text-client input limits and copy/paste checks |
| U13 | Wiki file metadata does not establish art redistribution permission | Preserve file-page links and game credit; record final asset-use decision before publication | Applicable game-art/fan-use terms or permission; no website publication occurs here |

Sources: [Doomsayer](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Doomsayer_(ToS2)), [secondary Doomsayer](https://town-of-salem.fandom.com/wiki/Doomsayer), [official R1.5.13](https://www.townofsalem.io/town-of-salem-2-bug-fixes-patch-notes-r1-5-13/), [Investigator](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Investigator_(ToS2)), [Coroner](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Coroner_(ToS2)), [Psychic](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Psychic_(ToS2)), [Serial Killer](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Serial_Killer_(ToS2)), [Keywords](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Keywords_(ToS2)), [Shroud](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Shroud_(ToS2)), [Spy](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Spy_(ToS2)), [Catalyst](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Catalyst_(ToS2)), [Vampire](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Vampire_(ToS2)), [Cursed Soul](https://townofsalem.wiki.gg/wiki/Cursed_Soul_(ToS2)).

## How to display uncertainty

- Quick cards omit speculative advanced rules or state the safe limited conclusion.
- The relevant research section shows a small “Sources disagree” or “Interaction not verified” note with the two claims and source links.
- A future interpreter can return “Need more context” instead of producing a guilty/innocent verdict.
- A stateful will editor preserves unexpected feedback and permits manual text. It must not overwrite it to fit an incomplete model.
- Resolving an item updates the source record, the deep explanation, quick advice, claim-fit conditions, template rules, and acceptance case together.

None of these entries requires stopping the planning task or asking the user to adjudicate mechanics. They are bounded content limitations for implementation and future validation.

editingRules: Start new matches with blank inputs; example numbers are never copied into live entries.
Public cover and private actual-role history are separate namespaces. Public export must read only the selected public draft.
Cover export uses its claimed-role heading and authored entries only; private notes, actual role and progression are excluded.
Failed/no result is distinct from a successful negative result; blank outcome stays blank.
Detailed export may add explicitly selected public entry notes; raw input is preserved.
Multiple actions per cycle are permitted; add-next-night uses the highest existing night number.
Role and faction transitions preserve previous action history. Advisory constraints never destroy manual client feedback.
sourceSummary.presentation: Ranked conditional opening routes with saved per-role choices and checkpoints; claim strategy bullets first, collapsible role basics, lower-priority icon previews, and illustrative wills.
